title: Recognition of edge-clique graphs
statement: An **edge-clique graph** is a graph obtained as the edge-clique graph $K_e(G)$ of some graph $G$, where vertices of $K_e(G)$ represent edges of $G$ and adjacency represents incident edges in $G$. **Recognition conjecture.** Determining whether a given graph is an edge-clique graph is an open problem. The paper notes that, as far as the authors know, no recognition algorithm or complexity classification is known.
source_name: Maw-Shang Chang, Ton Kloks and Ching-Hao Liu, “Edge-clique graphs of cocktail parties have unbounded rankwidth”, arXiv:1205.2483 (2012).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.2483

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2012). “As far as we know, the recognition of edge-clique graphs is an open problem.”
